heroText: Santiago sits between the Andes and Chile's central valley, mixing government squares, wine-country access and a fast-growing restaurant scene. Start at Plaza de Armas, ride up Cerro San Cristobal for scale, then spend an evening in Barrio Lastarria or Bellavista. Arturo Merino Benitez airport is the main gateway, with easy onward routes toward Valparaiso and the Maipo Valley.

areas.name: Lastarria
areas.text: Lastarria is the best first base for cafes, museums, walkable streets and easy access to downtown sights.

areas.name: Providencia
areas.text: Providencia is practical and well connected, with metro stops, hotels, shops and safer evening movement than the historic core.

areas.name: Bellavista
areas.text: Bellavista is nightlife-focused and close to Cerro San Cristobal, best for social stays rather than quiet nights.

areas.name: Las Condes
areas.text: Las Condes suits business travelers and upscale hotels, with malls, offices and easier access toward the Andes.

areas.name: Centro
areas.text: Centro is closest to civic sights and museums, but evenings are quieter and require more street awareness.

airports.name: Arturo Merino Benitez International Airport (SCL)
airports.search: Arturo Merino Benitez International Airport, Santiago, Chile
airports.text: Santiago's main airport sits northwest of the city; buses, taxis and pre-booked transfers connect it with Providencia and central districts.

airportTransfer.value: 25-45 min by taxi, shuttle or airport bus to central Santiago
airportTransfer.note: from Arturo Merino Benitez International Airport
airportTransfer.distance: about 17 km northwest of the centre

stayOverview: Lastarria is the easiest first Santiago base for culture and restaurants, while Providencia is the practical metro-connected choice. Bellavista suits nightlife, Las Condes works for business and Andes access, and Centro is best for daytime history walks.
hotelIntro: Santiago hotel choice depends on the trip rhythm: Lastarria and Providencia balance sightseeing and evenings, Bellavista is social, Las Condes is business-oriented and polished, and Centro is convenient for civic sights but less relaxed late.
rentalCars: Skip a rental car inside Santiago; rent only for wineries, ski areas, Cajon del Maipo or longer road trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Lastarria or Providencia for a first stay because both balance restaurants, metro access and major sights.

travelTips.title: Air quality
travelTips.text: Winter smog can hide mountain views, so plan viewpoints flexibly and check visibility before going up Cerro San Cristobal.

travelTips.title: Metro use
travelTips.text: Use the metro for cross-city movement, but watch bags closely at busy stations and during rush hours.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Valparaiso, Maipo Valley and Cajon del Maipo each need a different kind of day, so avoid combining them.

nearbyIdeas.name: Valparaiso
nearbyIdeas.label: Coast
nearbyIdeas.text: Valparaiso is the classic port-city day trip, known for hills, murals, funiculars and Pacific views.

nearbyIdeas.name: Vina del Mar
nearbyIdeas.label: Coast
nearbyIdeas.text: Vina del Mar adds beaches, gardens and resort-town energy beside Valparaiso, often paired on a long day.

nearbyIdeas.name: Cajon del Maipo
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Cajon del Maipo is Santiago's mountain escape for rivers, viewpoints and outdoor trips into the Andes.

nearbyIdeas.name: Maipo Valley
nearbyIdeas.label: Wine
nearbyIdeas.text: Maipo Valley wineries are close to Santiago, making wine tastings one of the easiest half-day plans.

history.text: Santiago was left vulnerable, and a coalition of Mapuche and Picunche tribes led by chief Michimalonco destroyed the city on 11 September 1541, despite the efforts of a Spanish garrison of 55 soldiers defending.
The city was gradually rebuilt, with the newly established city of Concepción gaining political prominence as the Royal Audiencia of Chile was established there in 1565.
During the 16th and 17th centuries, the growth of the city was hindered by a series of disasters including an earthquake, a smallpox epidemic in 1575, the Mapocho River floods in 1590, 1608, and.
However, the ongoing threat of the Arauco War and frequent earthquakes delayed the establishment of the Royal Court in Santiago until 1607, which solidified the city's status as the capital.

In 1851, the first telegraph system connecting the capital to the Port of Valparaíso was inaugurated.
Modernity also spread in the city, with the introduction of the first theaters, the expansion of the telephone network, and the opening of Los Cerrillos Airport in 1928, among other advancements.
The 1962 World Cup provided a new impetus for city improvement efforts, and in 1966, the Santiago Metropolitan Park was established on Cerro San Cristóbal.
In 1967, the new Pudahuel International Airport was opened, and after years of discussion, construction of the Santiago Metro began in 1969.
The first phase of the Metro, which ran beneath the western section of Alameda, was opened in 1975 and soon became one of the most prestigious buildings in the city.
On 27 February 2010, a powerful earthquake hit the capital city of Santiago, causing damage to some older buildings and rendering some modern structures uninhabitable.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The Incas established a settlement of mitimas in the valley, located in the center of present-day Santiago, with fortifications such as Huaca de Chena and the El Plomo hill sanctuary.
